steps.title: Aggression
steps.body: Behaviour that is intended to harm another person or object. In sport, aggression must be distinguished from assertion - assertion is forceful but legitimate play within the rules, while aggression goes beyond the rules with intent to harm.

steps.title: Direct Aggression
steps.body: Aggression that is aimed directly at another person, involving physical contact or confrontation with the intent to cause harm.

steps.title: Indirect Aggression
steps.body: Aggression that is not aimed directly at another person. It may involve verbal abuse, psychological intimidation, or aggression directed at objects rather than people.

steps.title: Personality
steps.body: The unique combination of characteristics, traits and behaviours that make an individual distinct. In sport, personality influences the type of activity a performer is drawn to and how they respond to different situations.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always distinguish between aggression and assertion - examiners test this distinction frequently Give specific sporting examples for each type of aggression, personality and motivation Remember: introvert ≠ shy; extrovert ≠ confident - focus on social energy and arousal preference When evaluating motivation, always consider both intrinsic and extrinsic together Know the overjustification effect - too much extrinsic reward can reduce intrinsic motivation Most performers have a mix of both motivation types - don't present them as either/or
